items.q: Match the diagnostic-algorithm branch to the printed result — 1) High C-peptide, Ab positive 2) Low C-peptide, Ab positive 3) Absent C-peptide 4) Absent branch label … A) T1DM B) LADA C) T2DM/MODY D) The algorithm does not add another result
items.exp: The flowchart maps high C-peptide with positive antibody to T1DM, low with positive antibody to LADA, and absent to T2DM/MODY. (Book p925)

items.q: A young patient reaches the page's diagnostic algorithm after clinical features suggest a young-onset diabetes form. What is checked next?
items.exp: The algorithm says clinical features plus young age, followed by checking fasting C-peptide levels. (Book p925)

items.q: Assess the pancreatic-DM cause list: I Tropical chronic calcific pancreatitis is listed. II IgG4-related disease is listed.
items.exp: The Type 3 DM cause list includes tropical chronic calcific pancreatitis and IgG4-related disease. (Book p925)

items.q: Type 3c DM on this page is identified with:
items.exp: The page labels Type 3c as TCCP, tropical chronic calcific pancreatitis. (Book p925)

items.q: The clinical-feature section places Type 3c onset chiefly in which decades?
items.exp: The Type 3c clinical features begin with second–third decade and younger males. (Book p925)

items.q: Match the Type 3c feature to its printed detail — 1) Ductal change 2) Cancer risk 3) Body/ketosis profile 4) Investigation … A) Large ductal calculi, duct dilation and marked fibrosis B) Increased risk of pancreatic cancer C) Lean young ketosis-negative DM D) ERCP gold standard
items.exp: The page describes large ductal calculi with dilation and fibrosis, increased pancreatic-cancer risk, lean young ketosis-negative diabetes, and ERCP as the gold standard. (Book p925)

items.q: The Type 3c clinical combination written on the page is DM with steatorrhea and abdominal ___.
items.exp: The clinical-features list reads DM plus steatorrhea plus abdominal pain. (Book p925)

items.q: Assess the Type 3c complications: I Nephropathy is listed. II Macrovascular complications are described as common.
items.exp: Nephropathy is listed, while macrovascular complications are described as rare. (Book p925)

items.q: Which procedure is labelled the gold-standard investigation for the Type 3c pattern?
items.exp: The investigation line labels ERCP as the gold standard. (Book p925)

items.q: Match the Type 3d drug-associated group to the example — 1) Immunosuppressant 2) Anticancer 3) Psychiatric 4) Diuretic … A) Tacrolimus B) L-asparaginase C) Olanzapine D) Thiazide
items.exp: The Type 3d list gives tacrolimus as immunosuppressant, L-asparaginase as anticancer, olanzapine as psychiatric, and thiazide as diuretic. (Book p925)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among the insulin-independent drug examples at the bottom of the page?
items.exp: The page places nicotinic acid, statins and aspirin under acting independent of insulin; tacrolimus is listed under immunosuppressants. (Book p925)

items.q: Which drug is listed under the endocrine group of Type 3d drug causes?
items.exp: GH is written under the endocrine group in the Type 3d drug list. (Book p925)
